title: Newton-Cartan limit of Klein-Gordon AQFT: spectral concentration and metastability of gravitational atoms (Corollary 1)
author:
Leonardo
Pachón
work: Newton-Cartan limit of Klein-Gordon AQFT: gravitational atoms and the loss of vacuum entanglement
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's spectral concentration and metastability corollary for gravitational atoms, printed as Corollary 1 at source0.tex lines 1171-1196 and delivered with the paper's own complete proof (lines 1198-1218). The statement gives the two facts a non-relativistic limit of a quantum field theory on a black-hole exterior is expected to produce: uniform convergence of the diagonal matrix element of the time evolution of a hydrogenic state to the hydrogenic phase, and concentration of the spectral measure of the evolved state at the hydrogenic level, with explicit rates in the gravitational fine-structure constant; it then records that at every finite speed of light the same state decays, so the bound states are metastable rather than stable. The proof is the paper's own assembly: it invokes the retained Schwarzschild theorem for the first two statements, repeats the retained approximants argument with the eigenfunction in place of a compactly supported test function to get the cut-off errors, converts the energy displacement into a momentum displacement, applies Duhamel's formula to bound the phase error, controls the spectral mass outside the interval by the squared momentum displacement over the window, and finishes with Wiener's theorem because the finite-speed operator has no eigenvalues. This is a source-local argument about a non-relativistic limit in a curved background rather than a qualifying-examination exercise; the unit is H2.
